title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1RC0RC_1LD0LE_1RA1LC_1LC0LF_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1RC0RC_1LD0LE_1RA1LC_1LC0LF_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its run is a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by two cells per tick, and tick k rewrites the word to the right of the block by applying one fixed map P to it exactly 2k times. P is a single trip of the head into the word and back. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The clock is proved in Lean for every k and every word: if P takes the word through 2k trips, the tick happens, in an exactly known number of steps. What P does to the word over many trips, and what happens when a trip does not come back (the end of a phase), is not proved. An exact accelerated simulator, checked against the direct one at every visit of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, follows the run through 28 phases past 5.792·10176 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 191 cells have been visited and 106 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text: The self-loops of the table cross runs of any length: sweep_A1, for every length and every tape around.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F on 1. F is entered only from E on 1 (0LF), and E only from C on 1 (0LE): the machine halts exactly when C reads a 1 with two 1s to its left, 1 1 C>1. Both directions are proved in Lean, by a case split on the cells the head reads: a configuration halts two steps later if and only if it is 1 1 C>1 (halt_iff_2), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_2).

claims.title: The sweep and the merge
claims.text: rule_sweep: 0 0 D> 1^(3+2n) 0 becomes 1 0^(4+2n) 1 B> (the block is swept into 0s); rule_merge: 1 0 D> 1 becomes D> 1 1 1, for every n and all tapes around.

claims.title: The clock, for every k
claims.text: tick: for every k, every word W and all tapes L, if W reaches W' by 2k P-steps (each one an excursion L 0^3 1 B> W → L D> 1^3 0 W') of total cost E, then L 0 0 D> 1^(3+2k) 0 W reaches L D> 1^(3+2k+2) 0 W' in exactly E + 12·2k − 2 steps. Strong induction on k: the tick is the sweep, one P-step, ticks 0 … k−1, and the merge. tick_left_end: the same at the left end of the tape.

claims.title: The exact accelerated run
claims.text: holdouts/1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE/py/clock.py simulates cell by cell, but does a tick at once when its 2k P-steps all come back (the theorem above; P computed by running the machine, P2k memoized on the part of the word it reads). It gives the same time, block and word as tools/c/tmrun.c at every visit of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, and follows the run through 28 phases past 5.792·10176 steps: no halt (an earlier version, which read unvisited cells of the word as 0s inside nested P-steps, was wrong after step 2.290·1014; a direct C run from the tape at the last visit where the two versions agree reaches the next visit 113,495,848,649 steps later, as the corrected run does).

claims.title: What the word does
claims.text: After a leading block 3 the word is a short binary counter in the digits 1 1 / 3, followed by a long block (1^9, 1^7, …) that shrinks by 2 each time the short counter wraps — a second clock inside the word. The longer blocks 1^17, 1^29 … are such second-level clocks; a P-step can contain whole ticks of them (the accelerator does those at once too).

claims.title: Rounds: the tape as a word over three tokens
claims.text: At the moments A stands on a new blank cell at the right end with a 0 on its left, the tape read from the head outwards is a word over V = 1100, K = 00, Q = 10, the tokens of the Coq proof of the sibling 1RB0RA_1RC0LC_0LD1RF_1RA1LE_1LD0LB_0RE--- (busycoq PR 48, not checked here). Rounds 0 to 19 (to step 6.2785·1063) have 3, 6, 12, 20, 30, 44, 62, 72, 102, 118, 164, 202, 232, 274, 310, 358, 422, 488, 558, 640 tokens. The same program reproduces the eleven words u0 … u10 of that proof for the sibling.

claims.title: The round is a transducer with a call count, but not the sibling's
claims.text: In directly simulated rounds 1 to 5 the head enters the leading V tokens 2, 7, 17, 37, 77, 157, 317, 637 times (n → 2n + 3); further in, K halves the count and some tokens turn n into about 3n/2. The sibling's rules only double, halve or keep, its word head is constant, and here the head grows and its separators alternate between K and Q with period 2. So the invariant of PR 48 does not carry over as it is; the transducer, its automaton and the potentials would have to be found for this machine.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: A normal tick cannot halt (the clock theorem). Halting needs a P-step that does not come back — that happens only at the end of a phase — followed by C on a 1 with two 1s to its left (1 1 C>1). Open: what P does over 2k trips (a counter in the word), what a phase end builds, and whether one ever reaches the halting configuration.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by two cells per tick, and tick k applies one map P to the word beside the block 2<sup>k</sup> times. The clock is proved in Lean for every tick whose 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return; an exact accelerated run follows it through 28 phases past 5.792·10<sup>176</sup> steps.

facts.text: Whenever its 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return, tick k = 2<sup>k</sup> trips P of the head into the word, in E + 12·2<sup>k</sup> − 2 steps.
No halt, in an exact accelerated run through 28 phases.
Halting needs a trip that does not come back and then C on a 1 with two 1s to its left (1 1 C>1).

sections.heading: A block that grows by two, each tick twice as long
html: Watch the tape each time the head, in state C, sits at the left end. It always reads C>0 1^L 0 W: a block of L ones, then a word W of short blocks. Within a phase L grows by 2 per visit and each visit takes about twice as long as the one before. From the real run:

Inside one tick the machine runs a recursion. The head sweeps the block into 0s, makes one trip into the word W (a P-step: it rewrites the front of W and comes back), and then performs ticks 0, 1, …, k−1 on a new small block, each one eating two of the 0s it left; finally it merges. So tick k contains one P-step plus ticks 0 … k−1: 1 + 1 + 2 + … + 2k−1 = 2k P-steps in all. The word sees nothing but P, applied 2k times.

This is proved in Lean for every k and every word (tick in lean/Clock.lean): if 2k P-steps of total cost E take W to W', then 0 0 D> 1^(3+2k) 0 W reaches D> 1^(3+2k+2) 0 W' in exactly E + 12·2k − 2 steps.

sections.heading: What P does to the word
html: From the phase start at step 273,305, one P-step per line (blocks of 1s):

A short binary counter (digits 1 1 and 3) runs in front; each time it wraps, the long block behind it changes (9 → 7 → …, then rebuilt). The word holds clocks of its own: later in the run blocks 1^17, 1^29, … appear, and a single P-step can contain whole ticks of such an inner clock. This nesting makes the run harder to accelerate: the exact simulator, which also does the inner ticks at once, gets to about 1023 steps in ten minutes.

sections.heading: A phase ends when a trip does not come back
html: The tick needs every one of its 2k trips to come back to the block. When one does not (the front of the word has run out), the clock breaks: the head goes on to the left over the half-built recursion, the block is dissolved into the word, and a new phase starts from a short block. sections.heading: Rounds, and a proved sibling
html: An outside Coq proof (busycoq pull request 48, not merged, not checked here) shows that the sibling 1RB0RA_1RC0LC_0LD1RF_1RA1LE_1LD0LB_0RE--- never halts. It looks at the machine once per round: when A stands on a new blank cell at the right end, the whole tape, read from the head outwards, is a word over three tokens, V = 1100, K = 00, Q = 10. During a round the head enters the first token a few times; each token passes on a number of entries to the next one, doubling or halving it; the entries that reach the far end are counted there in binary, and those digits are the clock of this page.
This machine has rounds of the same form (exact accelerated run, 20 rounds to step 6.28·1063):

But its word map is different. Counting the entries into each token in rounds run directly: on the leading Vs they go 2, 7, 17, 37, 77, … (n → 2n + 3), a K halves them, and some tokens multiply them by about 3/2, which the sibling never does. The head of the word grows and its separators alternate between K and Q from round to round, where the sibling's head is constant. So the sibling's proof is a plan, not a proof, for this machine: its rule table and its invariant would have to be found again.

sections.heading: What halting would take
html: The only halting transition is F on 1. F is entered only from E on 1 (0LF), and E only from C on 1 (0LE): the machine halts exactly when C reads a 1 with two 1s to its left, 1 1 C>1.

A normal tick never halts: the Lean theorem says it reaches its end. So a halt can only come at the end of a phase, in the trip that does not come back or in what follows it before the next visit of the left end. The accelerated run simulates exactly those parts cell by cell, and none of the 43 phase ends halted. Whether a later one does depends on the word the earlier phases built, which looks irregular: the question is open.

family: clock and word map (block grows by 2, the word is rewritten by 2^k excursions)
summary: A clock: at each visit of the left end in state C the block 1^(3+2k) has grown by 2, and the word to its right has gone through 2^k applications of one map P (one excursion of the head into the word) — proved in Lean for every k, for each tick whose 2^k trips all return; a phase ends when P fails to come back. Exact accelerated run: 28 phases past 5.792·10<sup>176</sup> steps, no halt. Halting needs C on a 1 with two 1s to its left (1 1 C>1).
